research_problem: Microservice API evolution challenges (communication, integration) are acknowledged but their underlying causes, coping strategies and research directions are unknown
technical_approach: 17 semi-structured interviews (11 companies) analysed with grounded-theory open coding, investigator triangulation, saturation and member checking; findings grounded in literature
primary_contribution: First practice-based catalogue of six microservice API evolution strategies and six challenges, theorised as tight organizational coupling and consumer lock-in
dataset_benchmark: 17 practitioners (developers, architects, managers; mean 10 years experience)
evaluation_metrics: Qualitative codes with participant support counts (i/17)
key_findings: REST ~67% of communication, all use OpenAPI; event-driven used by 13/17 but documented by 3/17; all avoid breaking changes and version APIs, 13/17 run multiple versions (2-8); only 5/17 treat behavioral changes as breaking; manual impact analysis, unknown consumers, consumers stuck on old versions (12/17), API quality degradation (14/17); proposed directions: automated change impact analysis and effective change communication
author_limitations: Limited generalisability (17 participants, 11 companies); possible misinterpretation mitigated by triangulation and member checking; findings below 5 participants omitted
analyst_limitations: Convenience/snowball sampling from authors' network; only 2 transcripts double-coded, no kappa; self-report without artefact triangulation; minor count inconsistency (4/19); REST/event-driven focus, no GraphQL/gRPC or LLM-agent consumers
reproducibility: Interview guide and codebook published; transcripts confidential
suggested_extensions: Behavioral breaking-change detection for REST; automated service-level change impact analysis; consumer-specific change notifications from gateway logs and OpenAPI diffs; AsyncAPI evolution/documentation tooling; LLM agents as API consumers; quantitative survey validation
evidence_location: Method p.2-3; RQ1 p.3-6; strategies p.6-10 Table 2; challenges p.10-14 Table 3; discussion p.14-16; threats p.16
integrity: Section order heavily scrambled by two-column layout; tables column-split; figures missing
